props.title: Mommie Dearest
props.initialSlug: Motherly love never looked so haunting.

sections.content: Mommie Dearest stands as one of Hollywood's most notorious biopics, with Faye Dunaway's explosive portrayal of Joan Crawford transforming what was intended as a serious drama into an unintentional camp classic. Based on Christina Crawford's controversial memoir, the film depicts the allegedly abusive relationship between the Oscar-winning actress and her adopted daughter. Dunaway's operatic performance - particularly the infamous "No wire hangers!" scene - has become deeply embedded in pop culture, overshadowing the film's darker examination of Hollywood's golden age toxicity and maternal abuse.

sections.content: The film spawned a subgenre of sensationalized Hollywood biographies that mix tragedy with excess. Frances (1982) followed immediately after, with Jessica Lange portraying the mental decline of actress Frances Farmer. Star 80 (1983) took an unflinching look at Playboy model Dorothy Stratten's murder, while Dragon: The Bruce Lee Story (1993) balanced reverence with melodrama. These films share Mommie Dearest's blend of celebrity exposure and psychological horror. SUBHEAD: The Legacy of Hollywood Tell-Alls

The impact of Mommie Dearest on celebrity biography films cannot be overstated. It created a template for exposing Hollywood's dark underbelly, influencing works like My Week with Marilyn (2011) and Film Stars Don't Die in Liverpool (2017). The film's examination of toxic mother-daughter relationships in Hollywood echoes through later works like Postcards from the Edge (1990), based on Carrie Fisher's semi-autobiographical novel about her relationship with Debbie Reynolds.
